sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The window was a steady climb with two step-ups: revenue growth of 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022 against 9.7% in FY2018 and 5.0% in FY2024 [D189][D238][D42][D336].
FY2021's 18% net sales increase came from a 16% comparable sales gain and new warehouses, with non-foods and e-commerce particularly strong [P56].
FY2022's 16% increase was driven by a 14% comparable sales gain, with gasoline, business centers and travel the fastest-growing businesses [P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of its 10.1% growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp and Canada 1.3pp [D670][D672][D679][D686][D434].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, or 10%, mainly on an 8% comparable sales gain from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of FY2026 revenue but contributed only 2.6pp of growth, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Operating income grew 12.3% a year against 10.0% for revenue, and FY2026 incremental operating margin was 4.7% [F204][F203][D457].
Operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 10.2% for cost of revenue and 8.9% for SG&A [D458][D449][D450].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, its window high, against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with cost of revenue flat at -0.0pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D447][D459][D460].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency increasing SG&A expenses [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.9pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap of 0.9pp [F52][F32][D448].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x, above the 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 operating cash increase came mainly from higher operating income and a reduced net investment in merchandise inventories, from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% against a 2.8% median, while capex of $6.4 billion ran at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [D418][D698][F92][D417][D423].
Stock-based compensation was 5.8% of operating cash flow, down from 9.8% in FY2022 [D424][D228].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, in FY2026, the 100th percentile of six retail peers against a -4.4% median [D427][D428][D715][D716].
Cash and investments grew 39.4% while total debt rose 6.5% to $6.2 billion, and the current ratio was 1.06x against a 1.02x median [D453][D454][D426][F182][D704].
FY2026 financing outflow of $3.4 billion covered dividends, buybacks, debt repayment and withholding taxes [P4][F122].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at 444.4 million [D429][D430][X100].
Operating margin of 3.9% sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin of 3.0% is also 17th against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].
The gap reflects a deliberately thin-margin membership model rather than deterioration, since the margin is at its window high [F32][D691].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% is only at the 50th percentile against a 4.2% peer median [D418][D713][D714].
Capex rising 17.0% in FY2026 and running 2.41x D&A is the pressure point to watch for conversion [D441][D423].
Whether operating margin holds at the FY2026 high of 3.9% or slips toward the 3.4% median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].
Whether free cash flow per net income stays above the 0.99x median from 1.02x in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D422][D701].
Whether capex growth slows from 17.0% in FY2026, with capex at $6.4 billion and 2.41x D&A, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D441][F92][D423].
